title: Transient Authorization Patterns and SIEM Ingest Strategy
body:
Purpose:
This note outlines a proposal for adding first-class support for short-lived (transient) authorization grants in the RBAC v2 design and a corresponding SIEM ingest and evidence automation strategy. The goal is to allow safe, auditable, and reversible delegation for operational workflows (on-call escalation, emergency maintenance, customer debug sessions) while preserving clear, machine-readable evidence for compliance reviews and incident forensics.

Scope and motivation:
- Problem: Permanent role bindings and long-lived tokens create noise in audit trails and increase blast radius. Many operational tasks require temporary elevation with explicit purpose and automatic revocation.
- Desired: A model where grants are explicit objects that carry TTL, scope, purpose, issuer, and linkage to evidence artifacts, and where audit logs and SIEM exports can reconstruct the full lifecycle of a transient grant.

Design principles:
- Principled minimum: every transient grant should answer who, what, why, when, and how long.
- Immutable issuance record: grant creation should produce an append-only issuance event with a unique grant_id.
- Short default TTLs with extensibility: default 1 hour for most grants, explicit extension requires re-authorization and is a new grant.
- Single-source-of-truth for revocation: revocation must emit a canonical revocation event tied to grant_id.
- Evidence-first: every elevated session should reference a justification artifact (human note, runbook id, JIRA ticket, or recorded video) with a verifiable hash.

Key concepts and fields (canonical model):
- grant_id (string): globally unique (uuid4) for each transient grant.
- principal_id (string): subject receiving the grant (user_id or service_id).
- delegated_by (string): subject that issued the grant (user_id or system service).
- grant_type (string): e.g., session, one-time-token, temporary-role, emergency-bypass.
- scope_list (string): comma-separated list of resource fingerprints (resource:action).
- ttl_seconds (string): original TTL issued.
- expires_at (string): ISO8601 expiry timestamp.
- justification_id (string): pointer to an evidence bundle (e.g., S3 key or evidence id).
- justification_hash (string): SHA256 of the evidence bundle at issuance time.
- issued_at (string): ISO8601 issuance timestamp.
- issued_by_ip (string): origin IP of the issuer.
- correlation_id (string): request-level trace id for grouping related events.
- revocation_event_id (string): populated if a revocation occurred.
- audit_event_ids (string): CSV of related audit events (create, grant-use-x, revoke).

Audit log schema additions (flat fields to append to existing audit events):
- event_type: grant.create | grant.use | grant.extend | grant.revoke | grant.error
- grant_id, grant_type, principal_id, delegated_by
- ttl_seconds, expires_at, issued_at, justification_id, justification_hash
- resource_fingerprint, action, effect (allow|deny), policy_version
- session_sequence (monotonic number when principal uses the grant within a session)

Example audit event (single-line JSON to be appended to audit stream):
{
  "event_type": "grant.create",
  "grant_id": "4b1f9b2e-9c3f-4c1a-8d0f-1b2c3d4e5f60",
  "principal_id": "user:aisha",
  "delegated_by": "user:raech",
  "grant_type": "session",
  "ttl_seconds": "3600",
  "expires_at": "2024-12-18T15:12:03Z",
  "justification_id": "evidence/2024/12/18/justification-789.hash",
  "justification_hash": "sha256:3a7f...",
  "issued_at": "2024-12-18T14:12:03Z",
  "resource_fingerprint": "model:prod-7:invoke",
  "correlation_id": "trace-998877"
}

SIEM ingest strategy and ECS mapping notes:
- Target index: redwood-auth-raw (raw events), then enricher pipeline writes to redwood-auth-ecs (ECS-compliant).
- Map canonical fields to ECS where possible:
  - principal_id -> user.name
  - delegated_by -> user.delegated_by.name (if SIEM supports nested, otherwise use user.delegated_by)
  - grant_id -> event.id
  - event_type -> event.action
  - issued_at/issued_by_ip -> event.created / source.ip
  - expires_at -> event.end
  - justification_id -> http.request.referrer or related.url (custom tag if needed)
  - justification_hash -> tags.justification_hash
- Enricher responsibilities (Kinesis/Lambda or Fluentd transformer):
  - Normalize timestamps to UTC ISO8601.
  - Validate grant_id uuid4 format.
  - Attach account/org metadata (customer_id, org_id) by resolving principal to directory.
  - Preserve original raw JSON in raw_event field for forensic completeness.

Evidence automation and storage model:
- Evidence bundles created at grant issuance: minimal JSON metadata + optionally attached artifacts (console snapshot, short video, linked ticket). Bundle stored in evidence-buckets/<org_id>/<year>/<month>/<grant_id>.zip.
- Bundle metadata stored in evidence-index (DynamoDB): keys: grant_id, justification_id, s3_key, s3_etag, created_at, hash, retention_policy.
- Retention policy: default 365 days for low-risk grants, 7 years for high-sensitivity operations (configurable by org).
- Automated attestations: for grants marked as "sensitive" (access to PII, billing, or customer data), require two-factor approval from an approver list; create an attestation record linking approver ids.
- Evidence integrity: store SHA256 hashes in DynamoDB and push signed manifests to our KMS-backed signing service so evidence can be verified during audits.

Operational telemetry and alerting (what to measure):
- grant_create_rate: grants issued per minute (by type).
- active_transient_sessions: count of non-expired grants currently in use.
- avg_ttl_by_type: average TTL observed per grant_type.
- grant_usage_latency: time between grant.issue and first grant.use event.
- failed_grant_use: attempts to use an expired or revoked grant.
- evidence_ingest_lag: delta between issued_at and evidence-bundle availability in S3.
- audit_ingest_lag: delta between event.timestamp and availability in SIEM index.

Rollout and migration plan (8-week phased):
Week 0-1: prototype
- Implement grant object and issuance API in auth-service behind feature flag.
- Emit grant.create and grant.revoke audit events to the existing audit stream.

Week 2-3: SIEM pipeline and evidence store
- Add transformer to normalizer to populate ECS fields.
- Provision evidence S3 buckets and DynamoDB index.
- Backfill scripts for mapping legacy temporary tokens to grant objects where possible.

Week 4: internal canary
- Enable for internal dev orgs and platform on-call flows. Collect metrics and run tabletop exercises to verify evidence completeness.

Week 5-6: expanded canary and compliance review
- Expand to a subset of customers (opt-in) and invite SOC/compliance to validate evidence and SIEM dashboards.

Week 7: migration tooling and dry-run revocations
- Provide migration tool for moving ephemeral tokens to grants. Run dry-run revocation tests to validate revocation event flow.

Week 8: GA with hard enforcement for new grant-based flows
- Flip enforcement behind a rollout flag for certain resource scopes. Continue monitoring and allow quick rollback.

Migration considerations and compatibility:
- Backwards compatibility: existing long-lived role bindings are unchanged. Transient grants are additive and can be used by new flows.
- Backfill tradeoffs: for older ephemeral tokens we may create synthetic grant.create events with best-effort justification pointers. These should be flagged as "migrated" and excluded from automatic retention shortening.
- Policy engine upgrades: policy evaluation must understand grant objects as a higher-priority decision path when present.

Risk analysis and mitigations:
- Risk: missed revocation events due to pipeline failures. Mitigation: local fallback checks in services read grant metadata from authoritative store (DynamoDB) and not solely from SIEM.
- Risk: evidence availability delay. Mitigation: block grant.use for "sensitive" grants until bundle uploaded and hash confirmed.
- Risk: increased SIEM ingestion volume. Mitigation: sampling for non-sensitive grant.use events and full retention for create/revoke/error events.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Should every grant require a justification_id, or allow lightweight grants for low-risk ops? (tradeoff: noise vs. overhead)
- What default TTL is acceptable for developer productivity? 1 hour vs. 4 hours.
- Which approvers are allowed to extend TTLs and by what UI/UX in the Console?

Checklist before GA:
- [ ] Auth service grant API implemented and unit-tested.
- [ ] Audit events emitted and validated against schema.
- [ ] SIEM enrichment pipeline deployed and ECS mappings verified.
- [ ] Evidence storage and signing service integrated.
- [ ] Canary dashboards and alerts configured.
- [ ] Migration scripts and backfill plan reviewed by Compliance.

Appendix: Suggested minimal schema (flat key list for audit event):
grant_id, event_type, principal_id, delegated_by, grant_type, resource_fingerprint, action, ttl_seconds, expires_at, issued_at, issued_by_ip, justification_id, justification_hash, revocation_event_id, correlation_id, policy_version, session_sequence

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc is intentionally pragmatic: it trades some additional complexity in the auth-service for clearer auditability and smaller blast radius.
- Feedback requested particularly on TTL defaults, evidence retention windows, and sampling policy for SIEM.
